## cfoai
# cfo.ai MCP

You are connected to **cfo.ai** — an AI-native financial planning workspace. This MCP exposes Ari's public product tools for you to call directly. You can both **read** a company's financial model and **change** it: create and edit scenarios, pages, table blocks, Canvas blocks, formulas, variables, dimensions, and data ingestion.

Model-editing tools change the live model immediately and record reversible changes in its
changelog. Connections, access changes, and outbound actions have effects outside model undo. Build from saved data, research, supplied numbers, estimates, hypotheses, or invented
assumptions. Clearly label uncited inputs and their basis in the model and handoff. Create missing
model objects and editable inputs as part of the work. A missing source citation does not block modeling.

## Read the reference before you build

cfo.ai has its own modeling method, described under "How a table shows the model" below: how tables show variables, dimensions, and fields, how a reference reads from the cell it sits in, and how a table's rows and columns are built. `inspect_skills` owns the built-in and workspace skill catalog. Use its `list` block to find a skill and its `instructions` block to read it.

Read `build-model` before creating or changing model logic, variables, dimensions, or saved tables;
`build-visualizations` before adding a Canvas block; and `import-model` before rebuilding a model
from a workbook or export. Each manual contains its complete reference in `SKILL.md`.

Workspace skills hold company-specific playbooks. Read the relevant saved guidance before substantial work.

## Calling convention

- A multi-action tool selects one operation with the block named for that action; single-purpose tools use their fields directly. Supply only fields supported inside the selected block. An `inspect_*` tool reads saved product state; an `edit_*` tool changes it.
- `target` identifies an existing object where the operation needs one, including the destination of a new block. Creation fields describe the new object: use the selected operation's `name`, `title`, `source`, or other published fields. On an update, `name` gives the selected object's new name.
- Supply `org_id` when selecting a workspace by ID or slug. If you belong to exactly one workspace, the server selects it automatically. Use `list_orgs` when the correct workspace is unclear.
- Tools accept an optional `_context` object — `{ layerId, pageId, timeZone, utcOffset }` — that mirrors the in-app editing context. Supply `layerId` for the active scenario, `pageId` for the current page, and `timeZone` or `utcOffset` when relative dates matter. Identify existing objects by readable names or references returned by an inspection.
- Model object selectors accept names, returned `Name#hex` disambiguators, or IDs unless the field states a narrower contract. A returned `Name#a1b` carries a prefix of the object's identity, at least three hex digits and unique among every object of its kind when the result was written; later creates can lengthen it, so a reference from an older result resolves while it stays unique, and a fresh inspection carries the current spelling. Ambiguous or unknown names return candidates when available. Each tool defines singular or plural targets, omitted/empty/null input behavior, and scenario defaults.
- Reuse pagination cursors unchanged with the same tool, action, target, filters, and snapshot. Each cursor field names the returned value to use and any special empty-string behavior.
- A saved table is created or reshaped with its complete visible `rows` and `columns`. A dimension path may use a bounded member `filter`, an ancestor `when` condition, or independent sibling `branches`. Inspection returns the same saved shape under `layout.rows` and `layout.columns`. Updates use `row_updates`, `column_updates`, and `cell_updates`. An `add_dimension_items` entry places a planned member `under` an existing inspected parent.
- A Canvas block reads model values through named `datasets`. Each dataset declares the same visible sh… [truncated]

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. # Heirloom public site: design and build brief

Build exactly this. It is the result of a research pass over about 90 reference sites. Where this brief and your taste disagree, follow the brief. Where it is silent, follow the rulebook at the end.

## 1. Job of the page
A visitor (a security engineer, a distro maintainer, an AI-agent builder) should understand in about 60 seconds that Heirloom did real work on its own and that they can verify any claim. **Sell proof, not patches.**
- Every competitor in end-of-life support (HeroDevs, TuxCare, Seal, Aikido, Chainguard) *claims* to patch. None publishes per-CVE proof of affected or not affected.
- Heirloom publishes a calibrated verdict per CVE × release line, receipts for each, and says what it could NOT prove.

## 2. Direction: "Conservation treatment record"
Django 4.2 is the *object*, and Heirloom is the conservator. The page reads like a museum conservation report crossed with an independent verification report (Jepsen analyses, The Markup's "Show your work").
- **Accession numbers:** each CVE is an entry `HL–4.2–001` … `HL–4.2–019`, ordered by advisory date then CVE id. Use en-dashes, set in mono.
- **Record fields:** Condition (the verdict per line) · Examination (calibration + gates) · Treatment (the PR, or the evidence issue) · Evidence (provenance, links).
- **The human question** is called "The conservator's query".
- **Figures are captioned** "Fig. 1 — The register", "Fig. 2 — …". Tables are "Table 2 — Backtest".

### Colour (CSS custom properties; light is canonical)
- **Page:** `--paper #F7F7F4`, `--ink #17181A`, `--muted #66645E`, `--rule #DAD9D3`, `--surface #FFFFFF` (sheet).
- **The register sheet only** (Fig. 1 is the only "paper" object on the page; real bookkeeping ledger paper):
  - `--ledger #EEF2EA`;
  - blue rules `--ledger-rule #C9D6E3`, aligned exactly to table row lines;
  - a double red margin rule `--margin #C8463D` at about 60% opacity, as two 1 px vertical lines after the accession column.
  - No other texture anywhere: no noise, no grain, no `feTurbulence`.
- **Verdict chips** (text on fill, 1 px border in the text colour at about 25%):

  | Chip | Text | Fill | Symbol |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | FIX READY | `#1F4720` | `#D8EFDF` | ✓ |
  | NOT AFFECTED | `#194168` | `#D3E3FC` | ○ |
  | UNPROVEN | `#7A4A00` | `#F6E6C4` | ? |
  | AFFECTED | `#9B1C1C` | `#FBE1D1` | ! |
  | NO PROBE | `#66645E` | `#ECEBE6` | – |

  Every chip shows its symbol AND its word. Colour is never the only cue. Verify AA contrast.
- **Dark mode** ("night reading room"): redefine every token under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`, plus a manual toggle (`data-theme`).
  - Values: paper `#121315`, ink `#ECEAE4`, muted `#A19E96`, rule `#2B2C2F`, ledger `#16201A`, ledger-rule `#24384A`, margin `#C8463D` at 50%.
  - Chips get dark fills with light same-hue text: e.g. FIX READY text `#BFE8CC` on `#173523`. Check AA for each.
- **Forbidden:** cream `#F4F1EA` with terracotta, purple, gradients on text, glows, glassmorphism.

### Type
- **Newsreader** (`@fontsource-variable/newsreader`, opsz axis) for display and text. **IBM Plex Mono** (`@fontsource/ibm-plex-mono`, 400/500) for data only: CVE ids, hashes, accession numbers, version strings, field labels, the meta line.
- Self-host, latin subset only, `font-display: swap`, preload the display font. Total ≤100 kB.
- Rules: display ≤ 6rem; tracking ≥ −0.03em; `text-wrap: balance` on headings and `pretty` on paragraphs; measure ≤ 72ch; `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on every number. No eyebrow labels above headings: field labels sit inline, in mono small caps.

### Seal mark
An SVG wax-seal monogram: a slightly irregular circle (8–12 soft lobes), a ring inside it, and a serif "H" (from Newsreader, converted to paths or drawn).
- One flat colour: `--margin` red in light mode, a lighter red in dark mode. No gradients.
- Used in the nav (24 px), the favicon (SVG plus a 32 px PNG), the OG card and the footer.
- No mascot or character.

### Motion (restrained; one orchestrated moment)
- **The single orchestrated moment is the campaign replay** (§3.3). Nothing else animates on scroll: no section fade-ups, no parallax, no scroll-jacking, no looping background effects.
- **Chip ink-in** (replay only): opacity 0→1 plus scale 0.96→1, 180 ms, `cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1)`, with a 30–60 ms stagger within a batch.
- **Sheet:** 280 ms, `cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1)`; exit faster (200 ms).
- **Press feedback:** `scale(0.97)` on `:active`, 160 ms ease-out.
- **Hover:** only under `@media (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine)`, and only colour or underline changes of ≤150 ms. Matrix cells don't animate on hover.
- **Reduced motion:** `<MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">`, plus a CSS fallback (`0.01ms` durations, `scroll-behavior:auto`). With reduced motion, the replay steps between states without transforms.
- Animate only `transform` and `opacity`. Never `transition: all`.

## 3. Page structure (single page `index.html`, plus `404.html`)
Use a 12-column grid with generous margins. Content is left-aligned at a report measure. The register may run full-bleed within the container. Sections are separated by fine rules and `* * *`, never coloured boxes or bento cards.

1. **Nav** (sticky, quiet):
   - seal + "Heirloom";
   - links: Register · Finding · Method · Query · Results · Verify;
   - right side: GitHub (repo) and the theme toggle;
   - on mobile it collapses to a sheet menu.
2. **Hero / abstract** (no hero image; the register is the visual):
   - **H1:** "Django stopped patching 4.2 on 7 April 2026. Debian 13 and Ubuntu 24.04 still ship it."
   - **Sub:** "Heirloom is an agent that keeps end-of-life software patched — and proves which old versions are actually vulnerable."
   - **Abstract** (one paragraph, every number from data): what it did with the 19 post-EOL advisories: N fix ready (candidate backport PRs, probe FAIL×3 → PASS×3), N proven not affected, N unproven with evidence filed, and 1 question asked whose answer it reused.
   - **Mono meta line:** `Record HL–4.2 · 19 advisories · 3 release lines · data generated <iso> · built during neatHack, Oct 10–12 2026`.
   - **CTAs:** "Open the register" (scrolls to Fig. 1) and "Read a backport" (PR #13). Text buttons, not pills.
3. **Fig. 1 — The register** (the hero data):
   - A real `<table>`:
     - columns: Accession / CVE + one-line title / Django 4.2.30 (upstream) / Debian 13 · 4.2.28 / Ubuntu 24.04 · 4.2.11 + Ubuntu patches;
     - use the exact distro version strings available in the data;
     - a row total (e.g. "2 of 3 lines affected"), as in curl's vulnerability table;
     - a sticky first column;
     - `<th scope>` everywhere.
   - **Cells are buttons** that open the receipt. Arrow keys move between cells (roving tabindex, one tab stop); Enter/Space opens; Home/End go to the row start or end.
   - **Filter:** a ToggleGroup above the table with live counts per verdict (e.g. `FIX READY 13`), in the style of Oxide's RFD filters.
   - **Replay scrubber** above the table: the single orchestrated moment.
     - Dated stops: 2026-04-07 Django 4.2 end of life · 05-05 · 06-03 · 07-07 · 08-04 · 10-01 "Ubuntu ships its CVE-2026-15307 patch" · 10-06 · 10-09.
     - Rows ink in as their advisory batch arrives. A play button walks the stops over about 8 s. It's an `<input type="range">` underneath, so it works with the keyboard.
     - An `aria-live="polite"` line reads e.g. "Aug 4 2026 · 15 of 19 advisories".
     - At 10-06, draw a thin connector (an SVG path in the margin) from CVE-2026-87890's row to CVE-2026-15307's row, labelled "stacked on our own backport · PR #21 on #20".
     - Put a small "query #6" marker on 15307's row.
     - **Default state on load is the END (everything visible)**; the replay is opt-in ("Replay the campaign").
   - **Mobile (<768 px):** one card per CVE (accession, CVE, title, three line chips), with the same tap-to-open receipt.
   - **Caption:** "Fig. 1 — The register. Every cell is a test run you can open." Add a legend for the five chips.
4. **Receipt** (the shadcn Sheet; right on ≥768 px, bottom below; content lazy-loaded):
   - **Header:** accession, CVE id, title, advisory date, link to the advisory.
   - **Condition:** a chip per line.
   - **Examination:**
     - the calibration triangle as a small figure: U⁻ (upstream before fix) FAIL ×3 · U⁺ (upstream after fix) PASS ×3 · this line → result, with the failing test ids;
     - gates C0–C4 as a checklist with their detail strings;
     - probe origin ("written by the independent porter, <model>" or "hand-written").
   - **Treatment:** the PR link with "probe FAIL×3 → PASS×3", plus a note when it applied precedent P001 or is stacked on #20. Or the evidence issue link with its reason.
   - **Evidence:** run id, Entire checkpoint id, neatlogs trace id (copy buttons), $ cost and minutes, raw logs link, and the reproduce command `heirloom report --cve <id>`.
   - **Behaviour:** focus trap, Esc closes, focus returns to the cell, and the URL hash `#HL-4.2-007` deep-links to an open receipt.
5. **The finding — Fig. 2** (told on the page, no scroll-jacking): three dated steps side by side on desktop, stacked on mobile:
   - Oct 1: Ubuntu ships its CVE-2026-15307 patch for noble;
   - Oct 6: Django discloses CVE-2026-87890 (bytes in spatial lookups), an amendment to the 15307 fix;
   - our probe on noble's tree: FAIL ×3.
   - **Claim sentence, verbatim:** "noble's CVE-2026-15307 backport leaves the bytes path that upstream closed as CVE-2026-87890; our calibrated probe shows it."
   - Then: "The probe is hand-written and calibrated on Django's own fix commits (FAIL ×3 before dd0558d1, PASS ×3 after)."
   - Link the raw logs. No exploitability claim, no other Ubuntu release.
6. **Method — "How a verdict is earned"** (The Markup style). The rule in display type: "Never trust a test that hasn't failed." Then five numbered stages, each with one sentence and the artifact that proves it:
   - Locate the fix;
   - Write an independent probe (the porter never sees the fix's code hunks);
   - Calibrate on upstream before/after (FAIL×3 / PASS×3, coverage reaches the fix, mutants caught);
   - Adapt and verify on the old line (fail→pass, no new failures);
   - Decide and publish (PR with a claim table, or evidence; ask once when a choice is real).
7. **The conservator's query:** a vertical dated timeline from `campaign_evidence.json`:
   - question #6 opened by CVE-2026-15307 (asked_at);
   - CVE-2026-84429 waits instead of asking;
   - answered `adopt-upstream-tests`;
   - precedent P001 stored (stored_at);
   - #20 applies it; #19 reuses it without asking;
   - #21 stacked on #20.
   Each step links its issue, PR or trace id.
8. **Table 2 — Backtest** (from `evals/results.json`): v1 naive vs v2 Heirloom on cases with known answers. Show accuracy (decided), **false NOT AFFECTED (1 vs 0, emphasized)**, UNPROVEN and escalation. Add one sentence on why a false "not affected" is the dangerous error, and one on the neatlogs detection that flags it.
9. **Stated limits** (as in Jepsen's limits paragraph; honest, short, a list):
   - candidate backports, not Django releases;
   - tests run on SQLite and PostGIS only;
   - UNPROVEN by design for what it can't exercise;
   - the 87890 matrix probe is hand-written;
   - the recovery shown was a worker killed during a harness restart;
   - the campaign's harness was fixed and restarted 4× mid-run, and each restart resumed from the ledger with nothing published twice;
   - the porter sees the advisory and upstream's test diff, never the fix's code hunks.
10. **Economics (cfo.ai):** measured model cost per CVE and machine minutes per CVE (from data), with pricing hypotheses clearly labelled "hypothesis". Links to the three read-only cfo.ai Pages (Base / Bear / Bull) and to `docs/business-plan.md`.
11. **Verify it yourself**, as a "front shelf" list in the style of Dynamicland:
    - all PRs (number · CVE · one-line title · line · FAIL×3→PASS×3);
    - all evidence issues (number · CVE · reason);
    - Entire: build sessions are linked from commit trailers. Show the command `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly)'`, plus the runtime checkpoints on every backport commit;
    - the neatlogs detections JSON;
    - endoflife.date/django as outside confirmation of the EOL date;
    - the repository.
12. **Footer / colophon:**
    - the seal;
    - "Heirloom — keeps end-of-life software patched";
    - fonts (Newsreader, IBM Plex Mono);
    - "Data generated <iso> from evals/*.json and the campaign ledger";
    - "Built with neatlogs · Entire · cfo.ai during neatHack";
    - MIT; repo link.

**404:** "This accession number is not in the register." Show a link back and the seal.

## 4. Data (no hand-typed numbers)
- First run `heirloom export --out site/data` (it refreshes the snapshot).
- `site/web/scripts/build-data.mjs` reads the files below and writes `site/web/public/site.json` (≤150 kB) plus `src/data/types.ts`. It fails the build loudly if a required field is missing.
  - `site/data/{campaign,matrix,backtest,events,index}.json`, `site/data/cve/*.json`, `site/data/line/*.json`;
  - `evals/campaign_evidence.json`, `evals/results.json`, `evals/results_live.json`, `evals/detections.json`;
  - the inputs table in `docs/business-plan.md`.
- **Scope:** the register shows the 19 post-EOL CVEs. Counts must equal the README first screen. Add a unit test (vitest) for that.
- **Links:** PR and issue URLs come from the data. A check script verifies each returns 200 via `gh api`.

## 5. Stack
- Vite + React 18 + TypeScript (strict) + Tailwind CSS v3 with CSS-variable tokens.
- shadcn/ui (Radix): Sheet, Table, Tabs, ToggleGroup, Tooltip, Badge, Button.
- `motion` with `LazyMotion` + `m` + `domAnimation` (never the full `motion` component).
- Magic UI number-ticker only if patched for `useReducedMotion` and `tabular-nums`; otherwise plain numbers.
- Lucide icons.
- No anime.js, no Vaul, no Aceternity effects, no animated grids or beams.
- Code lives in `site/web/`. Base path `/heirloom/`.
- Deploy with `.github/workflows/pages.yml` (checkout → setup-node 22 → `npm ci` → build → upload-pages-artifact → deploy-pages). Enable it once with `gh api -X POST repos/iamdflame/heirloom/pages -f build_type=workflow`. The URL is https://iamdflame.github.io/heirloom/. **Deploy a skeleton first** so the URL is live early.
- **Meta:** title "Heirloom — keeps end-of-life software patched"; description; canonical URL; OG and Twitter `summary_large_image` with `og.png` (1200×630, rendered by Playwright from an `/og.html` view: seal, the headline, a miniature of the register's counts); SVG favicon.

## 6. QA loop (repeat until clean; ≥3 cycles across B7a and B7b)
- `scripts/qa.mjs` (Playwright + Chromium + `@axe-core/playwright`) against `vite preview`. For each run:
  - **Screenshots:** 390×844, 768×1024, 1440×900, 1920×1080; light and dark; `reducedMotion: 'reduce'` once; the replay at its start, middle and end; the receipt open on desktop and mobile. Save to `site/web/qa/<cycle>/`, which is git-ignored.
  - **Keyboard flow:** Tab into the register → ArrowRight / ArrowDown → Enter opens the receipt → Esc closes → focus is back on the same cell.
  - **axe:** zero serious or critical violations.
  - **Console:** zero errors or warnings.
  - **Lighthouse** with the Playwright Chromium (`npx lighthouse … --chrome-flags=--headless`): ≥95 for performance, accessibility, best practices and SEO on mobile.
  - **Budgets:** JS ≤150 kB gzip on first load, fonts ≤100 kB.
- **Read every screenshot PNG yourself** and write the concrete defects you see (alignment, spacing rhythm, wrapping, contrast, orphan words, overflow, chip clipping) into `site/web/PROGRESS.md` before fixing them. Never claim something was verified unless the script or your own look at the PNG did it.

## 7. Rulebook (from the research; apply everywhere)
1. Use only these 5 chip colours + the 5 page tokens. Never `bg-blue-500` and the like: use semantic tokens.
2. Radii: chips 4 px, sheet 12 px. Pick ONE elevation per component (a border or a shadow, not both).
3. Hit targets ≥44×44 on touch and ≥40×40 in dense desktop UI. Each matrix cell button fills its cell.
4. Focus: `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid currentColor; outline-offset: 2px }`. Never remove outlines.
5. Use `aria-live` for replay progress and the filter result count. Every state change needs a static cue too.
6. Tooltips only ever duplicate information; nothing essential lives only in a tooltip.
7. No emoji used as icons. No "→" appended to link text. No 01/02/03 numbering except the Method stages and the timeline.
8. Pick links to show from the data, never invent them. If a field is missing, hide the row; don't print "undefined".
9. Lazy-load the receipt sheet code. Load no images except the seal SVG and the OG PNG.
10. Copy is plain and specific. Never write "revolutionary", "seamless", "cutting-edge" or "AI-powered".

# Heirloom

<!-- top:start -->
**Heirloom is an agent that keeps end-of-life software patched.** For each new upstream security fix it writes an independent probe, calibrates it on upstream's own before/after commits, proves on the old line whether the bug is there, and then publishes either a verified candidate backport or the evidence of why it could not decide.

### What it did, unattended: Django 4.2 after its EOL (b4-replay campaign)

- **19 post-EOL Django CVEs on 4.2:** **13** AFFECTED · **1** NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN · **5** UNPROVEN ([results_live.json](evals/results_live.json)).
- **13 candidate backport PRs**, 13 of 13 with the probe FAIL ×3 before → PASS ×3 after the fix: [iamdflame/django/pulls](https://github.com/iamdflame/django/pulls) ([#9](https://github.com/iamdflame/django/pull/9)–[#21](https://github.com/iamdflame/django/pull/21); [fail→pass](evals/campaign_evidence.json)).
- **6 evidence issues, no code,** for the rest: 5 UNPROVEN (it could not prove either way) and 1 NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN: [#3](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/3) [#4](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/4) [#5](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/5) [#7](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/7) [#8](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/8) [#9](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/9).
- **1 question asked:** [#6](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/6), by CVE-2026-15307 (`UPSTREAM_TEST_CHANGE`). CVE-2026-84429 hit the same kind and waited on it instead of asking again. The answer (`adopt-upstream-tests`) became precedent P001; CVE-2026-84429's [#19](https://github.com/iamdflame/django/pull/19) reused it without asking (and CVE-2026-15307's own [#20](https://github.com/iamdflame/django/pull/20) applied it).
- **Stacked:** CVE-2026-87890's fix rewrites lines that CVE-2026-15307's fix introduced (git blame `115ffd0463`), so [#21](https://github.com/iamdflame/django/pull/21) is stacked on Heirloom's own CVE-2026-15307 backport [#20](https://github.com/iamdflame/django/pull/20) (base `heirloom/cve-2026-15307-4.2`).

### The same 19 CVEs on three 4.2 lines ([matrix.json](evals/matrix.json), $0, probes reused)

| Line | AFFECTED | not affected (proven) | UNPROVEN | no probe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Django 4.2.30 | 13 | 1 | 1 | 4 |
| Debian 13 trixie | 13 | 1 | 1 | 4 |
| Ubuntu 24.04 noble | 8 | 5 | 2 | 4 |

**Ubuntu cross-check:** of the 5 of these CVEs that noble already patches, 4 come out NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN on noble (CVE-2026-35192, CVE-2026-5766, CVE-2026-6907, CVE-2026-8404); CVE-2026-15307 is UNPROVEN (NO_REACH) there.

**Ubuntu finding:** noble's CVE-2026-15307 backport leaves the bytes path that upstream closed as CVE-2026-87890; our calibrated probe shows it. The probe is hand-written and calibrated on Django's own fix commits (FAIL ×3 before `dd0558d1`, PASS ×3 after; FAIL ×3 on noble's tree; [raw logs](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/tree/82c160324de18f5da85166318a18891bb280f143/matrix/b4-20261011/CVE-2026-87890), [draft report](docs/outreach/ubuntu-cve-2026-87890.md), not filed).

- **Everything mapped to the hackathon's evidence list:** [EVIDENCE.md](EVIDENCE.md); Definition-of-Done check: [docs/DOD-status.md](docs/DOD-status.md).

### What's real / known limits

- These are **candidate backports, not Django releases**; nobody has reviewed or merged them.
- Tests run on **SQLite and PostGIS only**; backend-specific fixes (MySQL, Oracle, SpatiaLite) cannot be exercised.
- **UNPROVEN is by design** for what Heirloom cannot exercise: it publishes evidence, never a guess.
- The porter sees the advisory and upstream's test diff, **never the fix's code hunks**.
- The CVE-2026-87890 matrix probe is **hand-written** (the campaign's own 87890 probe came from the porter).
- The recovery shown was a **worker killed during a harness-fix restart**, not an injected fault.

**Built during neatHack:** all code was written during the event; first commit `a172b2d` on 2026-10-11 00:30:36Z. Build log: [hackathon.md](hackathon.md).

## How it works

For one CVE and one maintained line (here: the fork's `stable/4.2.x-heirloom` branch), Heirloom runs
LOCATE → PROBE → CALIBRATE → PRESENCE → ADAPT → VERIFY → BEHAVIOUR → DECIDE → PUBLISH, every stage
recorded in a SQLite ledger so a killed run resumes without repeating side effects.

- **PROBE:** an independent porter model writes a regression test from the advisory and upstream's
  test diff; a leakage guard refuses prompts that contain the fix's added code.
- **CALIBRATE / PRESENCE:** the probe must FAIL on upstream's pre-fix commit (U⁻) and PASS on the fix
  (U⁺) with stable failing ids, run cleanly on the old line, and reach the code the fix touches
  (coverage). Only then does its result on the old line count; otherwise the verdict is UNPROVEN.
- **ADAPT / VERIFY:** headless Claude Code (in an Entire-tracked worktree) adapts the fix to the old
  line without touching `tests/`; VERIFY needs the probe FAIL→PASS and no new failures or skips in
  the touched test labels.
- **DECIDE:** real choices (behaviour differences, upstream test rewrites) open one question issue;
  the answer is stored as a precedent and reused.
- **PUBLISH:** a PR with one claim per fact, each linked to its neatlogs span and run artifact (a claim
  missing either is struck), or an evidence issue when there is no verified fix.

# Heirloom

<!-- top:start -->
**Heirloom is an agent that keeps end-of-life software patched.** For each new upstream security fix it writes an independent probe, calibrates it on upstream's own before/after commits, proves on the old line whether the bug is there, and then publishes either a verified candidate backport or the evidence of why it could not decide.

### What it did, unattended: Django 4.2 after its EOL (b4-replay campaign)

- **19 post-EOL Django CVEs on 4.2:** **13** AFFECTED · **1** NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN · **5** UNPROVEN ([results_live.json](evals/results_live.json)).
- **13 candidate backport PRs**, 13 of 13 with the probe FAIL ×3 before → PASS ×3 after the fix: [iamdflame/django/pulls](https://github.com/iamdflame/django/pulls) ([#9](https://github.com/iamdflame/django/pull/9)–[#21](https://github.com/iamdflame/django/pull/21); [fail→pass](evals/campaign_evidence.json)).
- **6 evidence issues, no code,** for the rest: 5 UNPROVEN (it could not prove either way) and 1 NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN: [#3](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/3) [#4](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/4) [#5](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/5) [#7](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/7) [#8](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/8) [#9](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/9).
- **1 question asked:** [#6](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/6), by CVE-2026-15307 (`UPSTREAM_TEST_CHANGE`). CVE-2026-84429 hit the same kind and waited on it instead of asking again. The answer (`adopt-upstream-tests`) became precedent P001; CVE-2026-84429's [#19](https://github.com/iamdflame/django/pull/19) reused it without asking (and CVE-2026-15307's own [#20](https://github.com/iamdflame/django/pull/20) applied it).
- **Stacked:** CVE-2026-87890's fix rewrites lines that CVE-2026-15307's fix introduced (git blame `115ffd0463`), so [#21](https://github.com/iamdflame/django/pull/21) is stacked on Heirloom's own CVE-2026-15307 backport [#20](https://github.com/iamdflame/django/pull/20) (base `heirloom/cve-2026-15307-4.2`).

### The same 19 CVEs on three 4.2 lines ([matrix.json](evals/matrix.json), $0, probes reused)

| Line | AFFECTED | not affected (proven) | UNPROVEN | no probe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Django 4.2.30 | 13 | 1 | 1 | 4 |
| Debian 13 trixie | 13 | 1 | 1 | 4 |
| Ubuntu 24.04 noble | 8 | 5 | 2 | 4 |

**Ubuntu cross-check:** of the 5 of these CVEs that noble already patches, 4 come out NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN on noble (CVE-2026-35192, CVE-2026-5766, CVE-2026-6907, CVE-2026-8404); CVE-2026-15307 is UNPROVEN (NO_REACH) there.

**Ubuntu finding:** noble's CVE-2026-15307 backport leaves the bytes path that upstream closed as CVE-2026-87890; our calibrated probe shows it. The probe is hand-written and calibrated on Django's own fix commits (FAIL ×3 before `dd0558d1`, PASS ×3 after; FAIL ×3 on noble's tree; [raw logs](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/tree/82c160324de18f5da85166318a18891bb280f143/matrix/b4-20261011/CVE-2026-87890), [draft report](docs/outreach/ubuntu-cve-2026-87890.md), not filed).

### Backtest: does calibration help? ([results.json](evals/results.json))

| Pipeline | Cases | Accuracy (decided) | **False NOT_AFFECTED** | UNPROVEN | Escalation |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| v1 · naive (cherry-pick + LLM, no calibration) | 27 | 85% (27) | **1** | 0 | 0% |
| v2 · Heirloom (calibrated) | 27 | 94% (16) | **0** | 9 | 37% |

A false NOT_AFFECTED is the dangerous error (a vulnerable line declared safe). Full table, cost and per-case rows [below](#e1-backtest-django-42-2026-cves).

### Verify it yourself

- **Backport PRs:** [iamdflame/django/pulls](https://github.com/iamdflame/django/pulls). Every PR shows its verdict, the probe's FAIL on U⁻ and FAIL→PASS on 4.2, calibration logs, a neatlogs span per claim and its Entire checkpoint.
- **Evidence issues and the question:** [iamdflame/heirloom/issues](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues?q=is%3Aissue) (#10 is closed: superseded by #21).
- **Entire checkpoints:** build sessions on this repo's `main` commits (`Entire-Checkpoint:` trailers; `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly)'`) and runtime checkpoints on every backport commit, refs under `refs/entire/checkpoints/` on both repos. `entire review`, `recap` and `checkpoint explain` outputs: [docs/entire/](docs/entire/).
- **neatlogs:** traces live in the owner's private neatlogs org, so judges see the trace ids (in every PR and issue) and the detections JSON: [detections.json](evals/detections.json), [detections_flag_check.json](evals/detections_flag_check.json).
- **Business plan (cfo.ai, read-only):** [Base](https://app.cfo.ai/s/25vRDQClPxqPWB5g) · [Bear](https://app.cfo.ai/s/iY4Wmzs_IFo0SBTz) · [Bull](https://app.cfo.ai/s/ASqxTf1hUwtztmtT); inputs and sources in [docs/business-plan.md](docs/business-plan.md).

- **Everything mapped to the hackathon's evidence list:** [EVIDENCE.md](EVIDENCE.md); Definition-of-Done check: [docs/DOD-status.md](docs/DOD-status.md).

### What's real / known limits

- These are **candidate backports, not Django releases**; nobody has reviewed or merged them.
- Tests run on **SQLite and PostGIS only**; backend-specific fixes (MySQL, Oracle, SpatiaLite) cannot be exercised.
- **UNPROVEN is by design** for what Heirloom cannot exercise: it publishes evidence, never a guess.
- The porter sees the advisory and upstream's test diff, **never the fix's code hunks**.
- The CVE-2026-87890 matrix probe is **hand-written** (the campaign's own 87890 probe came from the porter).
- The recovery shown was a **worker killed during a harness-fix restart**, not an injected fault.

**Built during neatHack:** all code was written during the event; first commit `a172b2d` on 2026-10-11 00:30:36Z. Build log: [hackathon.md](hackathon.md).

## How it works

For one CVE and one maintained line (here: the fork's `stable/4.2.x-heirloom` branch), Heirloom runs
LOCATE → PROBE → CALIBRATE → PRESENCE → ADAPT → VERIFY → BEHAVIOUR → DECIDE → PUBLISH, every stage
recorded in a SQLite ledger so a killed run resumes without repeating side effects.

- **PROBE:** an independent porter model writes a regression test from the advisory and upstream's
  test diff; a leakage guard refuses prompts that contain the fix's added code.
- **CALIBRATE / PRESENCE:** the probe must FAIL on upstream's pre-fix commit (U⁻) and PASS on the fix
  (U⁺) with stable failing ids, run cleanly on the old line, and reach the code the fix touches
  (coverage). Only then does its result on the old line count; otherwise the verdict is UNPROVEN.
- **ADAPT / VERIFY:** headless Claude Code (in an Entire-tracked worktree) adapts the fix to the old
  line without touching `tests/`; VERIFY needs the probe FAIL→PASS and no new failures or skips in
  the touched test labels.
- **DECIDE:** real choices (behaviour differences, upstream test rewrites) open one question issue;
  the answer is stored as a precedent and reused.
- **PUBLISH:** a PR with one claim per fact, each linked to its neatlogs span and run artifact (a claim
  missing either is struck), or an evidence issue when there is no verified fix.

        distro: dict[str, Any], rec: dict[str, Any]) -> str:  # fmt: skip
    sm, per = live["summary"], live["per_cve"]
    v = sm["verdicts"]
    prs = sorted(sm["prs"], key=lambda u: int(num(u)))
    f2p = [x for x in ev["fail_to_pass"] if x["fail_to_pass"]]
    n_before = min(len(x["probe_before"]) for x in f2p)
    n_after = min(len(x["probe_after"]) for x in f2p)
    issues = sorted(sm["evidence_issues"], key=lambda u: int(num(u)))
    unproven = [c for c, r in per.items() if r["verdict"] == "UNPROVEN"]
    proven_na = [c for c, r in per.items() if r["verdict"] == "NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN"]
    (q,) = ev["questions"]  # the campaign asked exactly one question; fail loudly otherwise
    prec = next(p for p in ev["precedents"] if p["issue"] == q["issue"])
    reused = [a for a in prec["applied_by"] if a["cve"] != q["asked_by"]]
    asker = next(a for a in prec["applied_by"] if a["cve"] == q["asked_by"])
    stacked = [(c, r) for c, r in per.items() if r["depends_on"] and "/pull/" in r["link"]]
    ev_by = {e["cve"]: e for e in live["events"] if e.get("pr")}
    out = [
        "**Heirloom is an agent that keeps end-of-life software patched.** For each new upstream "
        "security fix it writes an independent probe, calibrates it on upstream's own before/after "
        "commits, proves on the old line whether the bug is there, and then publishes either a "
        "verified candidate backport or the evidence of why it could not decide.",
        "",
        f"### What it did, unattended: Django 4.2 after its EOL ({live['campaign']} campaign)",
        "",
        f"- **{sm['cves']} post-EOL Django CVEs on 4.2:** "
        + " · ".join(f"**{v.get(k, 0)}** {k}" for k in VERDICTS[:3])
        + " ([results_live.json](evals/results_live.json)).",
        f"- **{len(prs)} candidate backport PRs**, {len(f2p)} of {len(prs)} with the probe "
        f"FAIL ×{n_before} before → PASS ×{n_after} after the fix: "
        "[iamdflame/django/pulls](https://github.com/iamdflame/django/pulls) "
        f"({link(prs[0])}–{link(prs[-1])}; [fail→pass](evals/campaign_evidence.json)).",
        f"- **{len(issues)} evidence issues, no code,** for the rest: {len(unproven)} UNPROVEN "
        f"(it could not prove either way) and {len(proven_na)} NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN: "
        + " ".join(link(u) for u in issues)
        + ".",
        f"- **{len(ev['questions'])} question asked:** {link(q['issue'])}, by {q['asked_by']} "
        f"(`{prec['kind']}`). "
        + "".join(
            f"{c} hit the same kind and waited on it instead of asking again. " for c in q["waited"]
        )
        + f"The answer (`{prec['answer']}`) became precedent {prec['id']}; "
        + ", ".join(f"{a['cve']}'s {link(a['pr'])} reused it without asking" for a in reused)
        + f" (and {asker['cve']}'s own {link(asker['pr'])} applied it).",
    ]
    for c, r in stacked:
        e = ev_by.get(c, {})
        dep = e.get("depends_on", r["depends_on"])[0]
        base = per[dep]["link"]
        blame = (e.get("blamed_into") or [""])[0][:10]
        out.append(
            f"- **Stacked:** {c}'s fix rewrites lines that {dep}'s fix introduced "
            f"(git blame `{blame}`), so {link(r['link'])} is stacked on Heirloom's own "
            f"{dep} backport {link(base)} (base `{e.get('base_branch', '')}`)."
        )
    # matrix: the campaign's CVEs on 3 lines
    cells = [c for c in mx["cells"] if c["cve"] in per]
    lines = list(mx["lines"])
    count = {ln: Counter(c["verdict"] for c in cells if c["line"] == ln) for ln in lines}
    out += [
        "",
        f"### The same {sm['cves']} CVEs on three 4.2 lines "
        "([matrix.json](evals/matrix.json), $0, probes reused)",
        "",
        "| Line | " + " | ".join(SHORT[k] for k in VERDICTS) + " |",
        "|---|" + "---:|" * len(VERDICTS),
    ]
    for ln in lines:
        ver = distro.get(ln, {}).get("version")
        label = LINE_LABELS.get(ln, ln) + (f" (`{ver}`)" if ver else "")
        out.append(f"| {label} | " + " | ".join(str(count[ln].get(k, 0)) for k in VERDICTS) + " |")
    cross = [x for x in mx["summary"]["distro_patched_cross_check"]
             if x["cve"] in per and x["line"] == "ubuntu-noble"]  # fmt: skip
    met = [x["cve"] for x in cross if x["met"]]
    unmet = [f"{x['cve']} is {x['verdict']} ({x['reason']})" for x in cross if not x["met"]]
    noble = next(c for c in cells if c["cve"] == "CVE-2026-87890" and c["line"] == "ubuntu-noble")
    runs = {k: Counter(r["outcome"] for r in v) for k, v in noble["runs"].items()}
    out += [
        "",
        f"**Ubuntu cross-check:** of the {len(cross)} of these CVEs that noble already patches, "
        f"{len(met)} come out NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN on noble ({', '.join(met)})"

        f"PASS ×{runs['up']['PASS']} after; FAIL ×{runs['lt']['FAIL']} on noble's tree; "
        f"[raw logs]({NOBLE_LOGS}), "
        "[draft report](docs/outreach/ubuntu-cve-2026-87890.md), not filed).",

    out += [
        "",
        "### Backtest: does calibration help? ([results.json](evals/results.json))",
        "",
        "| Pipeline | Cases | Accuracy (decided) | **False NOT_AFFECTED** | UNPROVEN "
        "| Escalation |",
        "|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|",
    ]
    for name in ("v1", "v2"):
        b = bt["summary"][name]
        out.append(
            f"| {LABELS[name]} | {b['cases']} | {pct(b['verdict_accuracy'])} ({b['decided']}) | "
            f"**{b['false_not_affected']}** | {b['unproven']} | {pct(b['escalation_rate'])} |"
        )
    out += [
        "",
        "A false NOT_AFFECTED is the dangerous error (a vulnerable line declared safe). "
        "Full table, cost and per-case rows [below](#e1-backtest-django-42-2026-cves).",
    ]
    # verify links
    fail = next(s_ for s_ in rec["stages"] if s_["status"] == "failed")
    traces = sorted({s_["trace_id"] for s_ in rec["stages"] if s_.get("trace_id")})
    out += [
        "",
        "### Verify it yourself",
        "",
        "- **Backport PRs:** [iamdflame/django/pulls](https://github.com/iamdflame/django/pulls). "
        "Every PR shows its verdict, the probe's FAIL on U⁻ and FAIL→PASS on 4.2, calibration "
        "logs, a neatlogs span per claim and its Entire checkpoint.",
        "- **Evidence issues and the question:** "
        "[iamdflame/heirloom/issues](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues?q=is%3Aissue) "
        "(#10 is closed: superseded by #21).",
        "- **Entire checkpoints:** build sessions on this repo's `main` commits "

"""Writes site/data/advisories.json: title, date and URL of each register CVE.

Titles live in Django's docs/releases/security.txt, which the CI build can't reach, so this is
run locally (with the repo's own parser) and the output is committed next to the export.

    uv run python site/web/scripts/advisories.py [/path/to/django] [ref]
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from heirloom.sources.django_security import load

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
repo = Path(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/home/ubuntu/work/django")
ref = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "origin/main"
cves = json.loads((ROOT / "site/data/index.json").read_text())["cves"]
advisories = load(repo, ref)
out = {}
for cve in cves:
    a = advisories.get(cve)
    if a is None:
        sys.exit(f"{cve} is not in {repo}@{ref}:docs/releases/security.txt")
    out[cve] = {"date": a.date.isoformat(), "title": a.title, "url": a.url}
dest = ROOT / "site/data/advisories.json"
dest.write_text(json.dumps({"source": f"django {ref}:docs/releases/security.txt", "advisories": out}, indent=1) + "\n")
print(f"wrote {len(out)} advisories to {dest.relative_to(ROOT)}")
EOF

from typing import Literal
